fields.description: The three raised obsidian rim rings ringing the platform — climbable TorusMeshes whose tops form a height ladder for a sightline over the swarm. fields.description: Human-readable ability name (Missile Barrage, Laser Burst, Summon Reinforcements, Devour).
fields.name: title

fields.name: slug
fields.title: Slug

fields.description: Which arbiter ability family this is. missileBarrage and laserBurst are the cooldown-priority ranged pair; summonReinforcements spawns adds; devour is the slow apocalyptic finisher every royal gets.
fields.name: kind
fields.title: Kind

fields.description: Seconds between fires (or re-cooldown after a barrage). Missiles re-cooldown prince 2.7 / queen 2.0 / king 1.7 (boss.gd); summon interval prince 24 / queen 18 / king 24; devour fuse 60.0.
fields.name: cooldown

fields.title: Count

fields.description: In-window rhythm. Laser ability window is 4.0s (boss.gd LASER_ABILITY_DURATION) with bursts ramping toward the machine-gun cap; missile ability window 1.5s. Devour warning lead 10.0s before the sweep.

fields.title: Cadence (s)

fields.description: The projectile type this ability spawns (missiles / laser beam). Null for non-projectile abilities (summonReinforcements, devour).

fields.description: Human-readable royal name (Prince, Queen, King). Matches BossTypes.NAME in the Godot port.
fields.name: title
fields.title: Title

fields.description: Stable machine id (prince/queen/king) — the exact lowercase key the projectile layer's per-boss scalars expect.
fields.name: slug
fields.title: Slug

fields.description: Boss progression rank. 1 = Prince (floor 4), 2 = Queen (floor 7), 3 = King (floor 10, unlocks the next floor).
fields.name: rank
fields.title: Rank

fields.description: Base (pre-prestige, pre-floor) combat stats from BossTypes.HP / BossTypes.DMG. Effective stats compose prestige^killCount * 1.3^(floor-1).
Base max hit points. BossTypes.HP[type].

fields.description: Base contact/attack damage dealt to the player. BossTypes.DMG[type].

fields.description: Score / threat weight emitted on kill for the progression cluster. BossTypes.PRESTIGE[type].

fields.description: True only for the King — killing it unlocks the next floor (BossTypes.unlocks_floor returns true for KING).
fields.name: unlocksFloor

fields.description: The abilities this royal's arbiter can fire. References into the bossAbility collection. Order is the arbiter priority hint (missiles > lasers in the source).

fields.description: Base third-person chase distance (spring length). Source camera_rig.gd DISTANCE_THIRD_PERSON (3.0) / FRAME_DISTANCE_WIDE (4.5).

fields.description: Identifier for this loop document. There is one canonical loop — the order in which Coordinator.step() ticks every subsystem each frame.
fields.name: title
fields.title: Title

fields.description: The load-bearing per-frame update sequence from godot/core/coordinator.gd step(). Order matters: each system reads the just-settled state of the systems above it. The clock ticks first; every gameplay system then pulls the dt channel matching its semantics.
fields.name: steps

fields.description: 1-based position of this system in step().
fields.name: order
fields.title: Order

fields.description: The subsystem ticked at this step (the method called in step()).
fields.name: system
fields.title: System

fields.description: Which GameClock dt channel this system advances on. real_dt = unscaled wall clock (UI, camera, VFX). player_dt = real_dt scaled by slow-mo + death crawl. physics_dt = player_dt times the 1.2 game-speed (the world). enemy_dt = physics_dt hard-gated to 0 while the swarm is frozen.
fields.name: tickChannel
fields.title: Tick channel

fields.description: Why this system ticks here, and why on this channel.
fields.name: note
fields.title: Note
Tick steps

fields.name: slug
fields.title: Slug

fields.name: family
fields.title: Family

fields.description: Core combat stats, copied 1:1 from EnemyTypes parallel const arrays (HP / DMG / SPEED).
Spawn / max hit points. EnemyTypes.HP[type].

fields.title: Base HP

fields.description: Contact damage dealt to the player. EnemyTypes.DMG[type]. For the bomber/flyer families this is the detonation payload.

fields.description: Chase / movement speed in world units per second. EnemyTypes.SPEED[type].

fields.title: Move speed (units/s)

fields.name: statBlock
fields.title: Stat block

fields.description: Identifier for the clock document. There is one GameClock autoload — the single source of truth for time. It hands out four dt channels and never touches Engine.time_scale (which is too blunt: it would slow UI + camera + enemies uniformly).
fields.name: title
fields.title: Title

fields.description: The four dt channels GameClock exposes. Each consumer pulls the channel matching its semantics. Channels derive from one clamped real delta fed in once per frame at the top of Coordinator.step().

fields.description: The accessor name on GameClock.
fields.name: name
fields.title: Channel

fields.description: The math this channel applies on top of the raw clamped delta.
fields.name: scaledBy
fields.title: Scaled by

fields.description: What reads this channel and why it must use it.
fields.name: note
fields.title: Note
Time channels

fields.title: Game speed (flat physics speed-up)

fields.description: SLOW_MO_SCALE — the world/swarm run at this fraction of speed when bullet-time engages. Source: src/core/Game.ts:417 slowMotionTarget = 0.25.

fields.description: Human name for this on-screen HUD element, e.g. 'Health bar', 'XP bar', 'Chain-tier banner', 'Wave counter'.

fields.title: Title

fields.name: slug
fields.title: Slug

fields.description: Control kind: 'bar' (a fill / progress meter), 'counter' (a numeric readout), 'banner' (a transient toast / announcement), 'pip' (a discrete stamina / charge pip), 'icon' (a status glyph).
fields.name: kind
fields.title: Kind

fields.description: The game state or signal this element reads, e.g. 'PlayerStats.health', 'PlayerStats.xp', 'Coordinator chain tier', 'player.stamina', 'wave_manager.current_wave'.

fields.description: AAA-minimal styling note per the port UI philosophy — hierarchy + restraint + one accent, not flat all-cyan. E.g. 'cyan accent fill on near-black plate', 'hairline rule, no glow'.

fields.title: Driver

fields.description: The signal or per-frame feed that drives the overlay, e.g. 'player.damaged + Coordinator HP poll' (damage), 'Coordinator speed-ratio set_intensity' (motionVignette), 'Coordinator tier-crossing flash' (chainFlash), 'Coordinator.celebrate (King death)' (floorClear), 'GameClock.slow_motion_scale' (slowmo).

fields.description: Human name for this procedural sound effect, e.g. 'Machine-gun fire' or 'Level-up fanfare'.

fields.name: slug
fields.title: Slug

fields.description: The game ships NO sound assets — every clip is synthesised at boot into in-memory AudioStreamWAV buffers. These describe the procedural bake shape.
Primary oscillator shape used by the bake (sine, triangle, square, saw, noise) or a mix. Free-text — the bakes layer several partials.
fields.name: wave
fields.title: Waveform

fields.description: Fundamental frequency the clip is baked at, in Hz. Pitch-shifted at play time for tiered clips (kill thump, chime, chain-tier).
fields.name: freq
fields.title: Base frequency (Hz)

fields.description: Approximate clip length / decay time in seconds, e.g. 0.025 footstep, 0.15 ding, 0.52 fanfare, 1.2 dashboard-arrival chord.
fields.name: decay
fields.title: Decay / duration (s)

fields.name: synthParams
fields.title: Synthesis parameters

fields.description: Which priority pool lane the clip plays on. PROTECTED (2 voices) for long narrative clips that must not be cut mid-clip (fanfare, death stinger, boss-approach stings, Dead-Eye arm). COMBAT (6 voices) for short throughput clips (fire, impact, ding, footstep, etc.). Total 8 voices.
fields.name: voiceLane
fields.title: Voice lane

fields.description: The existing Godot signal Sfx lazily connects to (sfx never edits the emitter), e.g. 'combat.fired', 'combat.enemy_hit', 'swarm.enemy_killed', 'PlayerStats.level_up', 'player.damaged', 'crystal_collected'. Contract-only clips have no signal yet and are fired by a manual play_<name>() call.

fields.description: What this task is and why it exists. Markdown. Written at create time; the claiming agent reads this first.
fields.name: description
fields.title: Description

fields.description: Approach / architecture sketch, constraints, files to touch. Markdown. For a full design paper, set design_doc instead.
fields.name: design
fields.title: Design notes

fields.description: Primary design paper (paper doc-id). Expand on read with ?expand=design_doc to get the full paper inline when claiming.
fields.name: design_doc
fields.title: Design paper

fields.description: Definition of done. The closing agent must set met=true with evidence (commit SHA, test name, URL) per criterion.
fields.name: acceptance_criteria
fields.title: Acceptance criteria

fields.description: Set before work starts. Compare with outcome.actual_size at close to calibrate future estimates.
fields.name: estimate
fields.title: Estimate

fields.description: Soft deadline. Engine-inert — for humans and planners, not the ready sort.
fields.name: due_at
fields.title: Due

fields.description: 0 (highest) .. 4 (lowest). Drives bd-ready ordering.
fields.name: priority
fields.title: Priority

fields.description: Free-form scope tags. Agents: POST /v1/tasks/:id/labels {add,remove} (union semantics).
fields.name: labels
fields.title: Labels

fields.description: Doc-id of the parent task (a goal is a root task; this task is one rail of its parent). Plain string, may carry a drafts. prefix.
fields.name: parent_id
fields.title: Parent task

fields.description: open | in_progress | blocked | done | cancelled. Engine-written by claim/close/sweep; agents do not set in_progress by hand.
fields.name: lifecycle_status
fields.title: Lifecycle

fields.description: Worker id holding the claim. Engine-written on claim, cleared on lease reap. Close does NOT clear it (last worker stays attributed).
fields.name: assignee
fields.title: Assignee

fields.description: Append-only progress journal. Each claiming agent reads this for handoff context and appends terse entries (decisions, obstacles). Keep entries short — this is not compacted.
fields.name: worklog
fields.title: Worklog

fields.description: What this task is waiting for. Set when closing with lifecycle_status=blocked, or when filing a blocks edge.
fields.name: blocked_reason
fields.title: Blocked on

fields.description: mediaAsset doc-ids: screenshots, logs, exports produced while working. Arrays of references do not server-expand; fetch each by id.
fields.name: attachments
fields.title: Attachments

fields.description: Written at close. summary = what shipped/changed; resolution = how it ended; actual_size = calibration vs estimate.size; commits = SHAs / PR URLs.
fields.name: outcome
fields.title: Outcome

fields.description: One-line close rationale. For the full close-out use outcome.
fields.name: close_reason
fields.title: Close reason

fields.description: One-paragraph retrospective: surprises, estimate drift, advice for the next agent on sibling tasks.
fields.name: retro
fields.title: Retro

fields.description: Discriminator; always "task". Everything is a task — a goal is a root task.
fields.name: kind
fields.title: Kind

fields.description: Lease + fencing token. Read claim.epoch and pass it as observed_epoch on close. API is the single writer.
fields.name: claim
fields.title: Claim (engine)

fields.description: DEAD KEY — do not write. Real dependencies are task_edges rows: POST /v1/tasks/edges {from_id,to_id,kind:"blocks"}.
fields.name: dependencies
fields.title: Dependencies (legacy)

fields.description: Paper doc-ids (= slugs) linked via POST /v1/tasks/:id/papers {add,remove}. For the primary design doc use design_doc (an expandable reference).
fields.name: papers
fields.title: Linked papers

fields.description: Compactor-managed event tail. Live audit log is mutation_events, not this key.
fields.name: history
fields.title: History (engine)

fields.description: Compaction rollup: event_count, first/last ts, status_transitions, workers.
fields.name: history_summary
fields.title: History summary (engine)

crossValidations.name: done_needs_outcome
crossValidations.title: A finished task should record an outcome summary

crossValidations.name: blocked_needs_reason
crossValidations.title: A blocked task should say what it is blocked on

crossValidations.name: claimed_has_worker

fields.description: Human name for the theme singleton — the one palette + type system the whole game wears. AAA-minimal: hierarchy and restraint over a flat all-cyan data dump.

fields.title: Title

fields.name: accent
fields.title: Accent

fields.description: Named supporting colours pulled from the live arena — the neon/cyber set the world is actually lit and tinted with. Source nagrand_arena.gd (sky presets, beacon palette, floor accent, mote tints, mountain silhouette).
fields.name: palette

fields.description: Role of this colour, e.g. 'dusk-sky', 'floor-accent', 'beacon-gold', 'beacon-red', 'mote-cyan', 'mote-purple', 'silhouette'.
fields.name: name
fields.title: Name

fields.description: The colour value for this role.
fields.name: color
fields.title: Color
Palette

fields.description: Type system — sans for headings, the same sans for body (the port's HUD/menus stay sans-only; serif body is the doc-system convention, not the in-game UI).
Display / heading typeface for menu titles and HUD labels.
fields.name: heading
fields.title: Heading font

fields.description: Body / data typeface for HUD readouts and menu copy.
fields.name: body
fields.title: Body font

fields.name: fonts
fields.title: Fonts

fields.description: Human name of this temporal state (NORMAL, SLOW_MO, FROZEN, HIT_STOP, DEATH, FOCUS_DASH, CELEBRATION_SLOW_MO). Exactly one TimeState is active at a time, set via GameClock.set_time_state; each maps to a slow-mo target scale + a freeze decision applied every tick.
fields.name: title
fields.title: Title

fields.description: URL-safe identifier for this state.
fields.name: slug
fields.title: Slug

fields.description: The eased slow-motion factor (slow_motion_target) this state drives. 1.0 = real time, 0.25 = bullet-time. player_dt = real_dt * this * (0.01 if is_dead).
fields.name: playerScale
fields.title: Player scale

fields.description: Effective world-speed multiplier on real_dt for this state, i.e. playerScale * game_speed (1.2). Documents what physics_dt resolves to relative to wall-clock under this state.
fields.name: physicsScale
fields.title: Physics scale

fields.description: Effective swarm-speed multiplier on real_dt for this state. Equals physicsScale unless freezeEnemies is true, in which case enemy_dt is 0.0 and the swarm halts.
fields.name: enemyScale
fields.title: Enemy scale

fields.description: When true, enemies_frozen is set and enemy_dt returns 0.0 — the swarm hangs in place while the player and other channels keep ticking.
fields.name: freezeEnemies
fields.title: Freeze enemies

fields.description: How long a TIMED state holds before auto-restoring to NORMAL (counted down on real dt in tick). 0 means hold until explicitly changed (NORMAL / FROZEN are held, not timed).
fields.name: duration
fields.title: Duration (real seconds)

fields.description: Exponential ease rate (per real second) driving slow_motion_scale toward the target on entry. SLOW_LERP_RATE is 8.0 for normal eases; HIT_STOP SNAPS instead (no ease) because its ~60 ms window is far shorter than the ~1/8 s ease time-constant.
fields.name: easeIn
fields.title: Ease-in rate

fields.description: Exponential ease rate (per real second) ramping slow_motion_scale back toward 1.0 when the state releases. SLOW_LERP_RATE is 8.0 — the ease runs on real dt so the transition can never slow itself.
fields.name: easeOut
fields.title: Ease-out rate
